decisions.policy_decision: SUPPORTED variant: affectus/effectus lexical replacement plus received spelling and short-cue difference

decisions.policy_decision: SUPPORTED tiny variant under existing no-new-authorship criterion: exactly one formulaic added word, semper, plus separately recorded conventional conclusion difference
complete_body_findings: Whole Veronense lines 24–25 in Mense Octobri,XXXII De siccitate temporis read. Actual words have corpori and sanguini; manuscript apparatus note 11 sangui is not substituted into the main printed text. Printed omp/Ds abbreviations are expanded explicitly.

Entire target petition agrees except one added semper immediately before numeremur. There is no hidden rephrasing or omitted clause. Gelasian sibling atAP111 / printed18 uses corpore and reordered membra; it is not the controlling source and is not silently substituted.

Actual old cue is per.; target actual conclusion is Qui vivit et regnat in saecula saeculorum. Conventional conclusion difference must remain explicit, and source may not be described as printing target formula. AP156 establishes Sunday V heading, AP157 continues the same form, AP158 supplies complete Postcommunion prayer.
decisions.english_fidelity: Faithful to finite target variant, including always for added semper and the conventional target conclusion. No English correction required.
decisions.policy_issue: The added semper is an addition, not a substitution. Its one-word formulaic use adds no protectable composition. This applies the governing no-new-authorship criterion and existing local practice: the admitted NativityNight offering prayer expressly adds the interjected quaesumus while dropping tua gratia largiente (postconciliar-proper-translations-v1.toml, entry Grata tibi sit, Domine). The variant category must preserve the precise added word and this finite judgment, not imply verbatim body identity or permit recompositions.

decisions.policy_decision: SUPPORTED verbatim petition; different conventional conclusion cues explicitly outside body identity

Secondary target heading In Baptismate Domini, first principal Collect, Vel:, then this prayer directly establish occurrence 2. Relation verbatim is a petition/body relation, not identity of all printed conclusion bytes.

conclusion: All five source/English candidates are supported for unapproved project-created study English with all finite body and conclusion differences explicit. No English correction required. Exact authenticated 2008 claims remain unsupported.
policy_interpretation: Variant examples list substitutions and inflections; the governing criterion and existing formulaic-addition precedent permit the single explicit semper addition without new authorship. This is a bounded editorial application, not a new general similarity threshold or a reproduction grant for protected modern compositions.
